predecessors.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
predecessors.text: the province of Katanga: 'proclaimed its independence from Congo-Léopoldville on 11 July 1960 under Moïse Tshombe'

successors.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
successors.text: 'on 17 January 1963, Tshombe surrendered his final stronghold of Kolwezi, effectively ending the Katangese secession'

ledger.x: 1960: Moïse Tshombe declares Katanga independent from the Congo, eleven days after its independence.
By 10 January 1961 'Stanleyville forces had occupied northern Katanga as far in as Manono' without resistance.
January 1962: the Stanleyville regime ends and the page is silent on the strip; it is placed back in the Katanga claim until January 1963 (confidence 1).
January 1963: the State of Katanga ends; its land passes to the Congo (identity.successors).

wars.name: Katanga secession in the Congo Crisis
wars.outcome: The secession ended on 17 January 1963 with the surrender of Kolwezi; Katanga was reintegrated into the Congo.

wars.name: UN operations in Katanga
wars.outcome: Operation Rum Punch (August 1961) took 81 mercenaries; Operation Morthor began 13 September 1961 (13 UN troops and 200 Katangese killed); Operation Unokat in early December 1961; Operation Grandslam on 28 December 1962; Tshombe signed the Kitona Declaration…

certainty.note: The claimed frontier is the old province boundary; the pages do not place the clashes of the north ('from late 1960 onwards') or the UN's gains, so control of the north and of Élisabethville after December 1961 is approximate.

sources.title: United Nations Operation in the Congo
